deck_title: Barrow-Snell oblique apparent depth vs naive paraxial d_true/n overestimation rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic Isaac Barrow (1669, Lectiones Opticae) & Snell-Descartes oblique virtual-image apparent depth law (d_app = d_true * (n_air * cos(theta_o)) / (n_water * cos(theta_i)), accounting for oblique Snell refraction so the predicted-to-exact apparent depth ratio locks at d/d_exact = 1.0000x across all 17 viewing-obliquity stations u in [0.0000, 1.0000] with 0/17 distorted stations) versus naive paraxial constant-IOR depth scaling (d_naive = d_true / n, which ignores the cos(theta_o)/cos(theta_i) virtual-image elevation at oblique angles and overestimates apparent depth by 1 + u to 1.2500x at u=0.25, 1.5000x at u=0.50, and 2.0000x at u=1.00 across 16/17 stations) and 64-ray virtual caustic intersection tracing.
